context.faq_text: Recruitment Workflows let organizations set rule-based logic that decides what happens when someone clicks Apply or Register on an opportunity. To activate: go to the opportunity's Recruitment tab and click 'Enable dynamic workflow'. Each rule is IF-THEN: a Name, optional Conditions, and an Action. Rules are evaluated in order, top to bottom. The first rule whose conditions match the user determines the action taken. Conditions include: Active in Database, Completed a Sequence, Approved for an Opportunity, Approved in the Same Category, Age Restriction, Site Association, Profile Tags. Actions: Submit a Vome form, Form + request approval, Form + auto-approve, Request approval, Auto-approve opportunity, Redirect to external URL, Not eligible. A rule with no conditions is a catch-all and will always match, so place it last.

note: The FAQ says nothing about the feature being free. A script claiming it is has invented a public pricing statement.

context.faq_text: Admins can drag a volunteer from the roster panel directly onto a shift block in the week view, and drag between shifts to reassign. Overlapping assignments are rejected with an inline warning on the target block.

note: A long FAQ. The script still has to come in under 45 seconds, which means choosing rather than listing.

context.faq_text: Sequence steps can carry automations: a trigger and an action. Triggers include step assigned, step completed, step expired, deadline approaching, and status changed. Actions include send an email, send a push notification, assign a tag, remove a tag, move to another sequence, notify a coordinator, notify a watcher, mark the volunteer inactive, and create a profile note. Automations run in order. Each automation can carry conditions on profile tags, sites, age and prior opportunity approval. Automations are per step, not per sequence.

note: The FAQ itself uses em dashes. They must not survive into the script; the house rule is absolute.
